workload.note: embedding model: prefill+norm+mean-pool only, no decode/LM-head/sampling

roofline_basis: 3.72 TFLOP matmul (all 5 roles BFP4/LoFi) / 580.9 TFLOPS measured P150 BFP4-LoFi peak (tech_reports/GEMM_FLOPS)
named_limitations: bs>=8 MinimalMatmul is 55% of device time at 48% of BFP4/LoFi peak; every block above (8,8,8) exceeds L1 (3.03 MB dataflow buffers vs 1.57 MB) and the grid is already at the device max of 120 cores

bs>=8 runs entirely dram_interleaved: a bs32 activation is 41.9 MB. Forcing TT_BATCHED_L1_PREFILL with caps of 24/32 MB and MM blocks shrunk to 4,4,4 / 4,8,8 / 6,8,8 all fail with 'statically allocated dataflow buffers clash with L1 buffer'
legacy MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast rejected for batch: bs8 220.2 vs 189.3 ms, bs32 868.9 vs 707.2 ms, so minimal_matmul is correct at batch while legacy is correct at bs=1
MLP prefill chunking rejected: bs32 705.8 -> 746.1 (chunk 4096) -> 780.7 ms (2048), and raising the batched-L1 cap alongside did not help
core count is not a lever at bs=1: grid swept three ways (QWEN_MM_GRID, find_prefill_grid caps, QKV 8x8) all flat 28.8-29.0 ms; those rows already run at 69-70% of peak
bs=1 is device-bound with every op L1-resident (1.2 ms of 27.0 is dispatch), so fused-kernel approaches such as tt-blaze have little headroom to recover there
device is harvested 120/130 cores, so absolute numbers are ~8% pessimistic vs a full P150
